body:
### Problem

On macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 26.5), several `nvim --embed` server processes were left orphaned (PPID 1, reparented to launchd) after their builtin-TUI parents exited. Each orphan consumed ~100% of one CPU core continuously (observed for days, until killed).

`sample` of the stuck processes consistently shows:

```
getout
└─ os_exit
   └─ event_teardown
      └─ loop_close
         └─ uv_walk
            ├─ loop_walk_cb
            └─ uv_is_closing
```

i.e. the process is stuck inside the `uv_walk()` force-close fallback in `loop_close()` (`src/nvim/event/loop.c`).

The existing 2-second teardown timeout in `loop_close()` is ineffective in this state: it is only checked **after** `uv_walk()` returns, and `uv_walk()` never returns when the libuv `handle_queue` is cyclic/corrupted. The timeout was added precisely to guarantee a bounded exit (#11821, #11820), but this code path bypasses it.

A minimal C reproducer shows that a cyclic `handle_queue` makes `uv_walk()` spin at ~100% CPU forever, matching the observed stack signature exactly:

```c
#include <uv.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static void walk_cb(uv_handle_t *h, void *arg) {
  if (!uv_is_closing(h)) uv_close(h, NULL);
}
static void noop(uv_timer_t *h) {}
int main(void) {
  uv_loop_t loop; uv_loop_init(&loop);
  uv_timer_t t[3];
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    uv_timer_init(&loop, &t[i]);
    uv_timer_start(&t[i], noop, 100000, 0);
  }
  // Fault injection: make the intrusive handle queue cyclic (models the
  // corrupted state observed in the stuck processes).
  t[1].handle_queue.next = t[0].handle_queue.next;
  t[1].handle_queue.prev = t[0].handle_queue.prev;
  uv_walk(&loop, walk_cb, NULL);  // never returns, ~100% CPU
  return 0;
}
```

Fixing libuv's `uv_walk()` itself is not viable: with an already-corrupted intrusive linked list there is no safe recovery, and even a bounded walk can still crash afterwards. The defense belongs in Nvim's exit path: do not call `uv_walk()` (which force-closes unknown luv handles anyway), keep `UV_RUN_NOWAIT`, and let the existing timeout fire so the process always exits, logging the remaining handles via `log_uv_handles()`.

A local patch removing the `uv_walk()` fallback from `loop_close()` builds cleanly, passes `make lintc`, the startup/exit functional tests, and the TUI `:detach` tests on current master. Trade-off: a plugin that leaks an active libuv handle now costs ~2s + exit code 1 with a logged handle list, instead of being silently force-closed.

I was unable to determine how the `handle_queue` becomes cyclic through supported Nvim API usage (see below), so this report intentionally covers the hang + timeout bypass; the underlying corruption source is still unknown.

### Steps to reproduce

The actual trigger is **not reproducible on demand**. Evidence from the real occurrences:

- Five independent `nvim --embed` orphans across different projects/sessions, all with the same `loop_close → uv_walk` spin stack.
- Each held different resources (0–12 unix sockets, 0–22 swap files, 5 kqueues), so no single plugin/resource type is common to all.
- stdio fds 0/1/2 were kernel-revoked; the parent TUI PIDs were gone.
- Hundreds of stress attempts did **not** reproduce the queue corruption: `--clean` and full-config `:qall!`, killing the TUI parent with SIGKILL/SIGHUP/SIGTERM, rapid pty teardown, hundreds of timers/signals/FSEvents watchers, many buffers+swap files, Snacks explorer, LSP, and GC churn.

The C reproducer above demonstrates the spin mechanism and is provided as the smallest faithful model; it is not the corruption source.

### Expected behavior

The exit path must be bounded even when a handle cannot be closed:

- `loop_close()` should never depend on `uv_walk()` returning; the existing 2s timeout must always be reachable.
- On timeout, log remaining handles (`log_uv_handles()`) and exit.

Consider dropping the `uv_walk()` force-close fallback entirely (it also cannot run resource-specific close callbacks, per the existing `XXX` comment), or bounding it so teardown always terminates.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.4
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1785763465

Current master (`e8a1addb5`, v0.13.0-dev-1307) still contains the same `loop_close()` structure (verified by source inspection); the hang was not reproduced on master.

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

n/a (not a Vim issue; relates to Nvim's `loop_close()`/libuv teardown)

### Operating system/version

macOS 26.5, Apple Silicon (arm64)

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

Homebrew (`neovim` 0.12.4, `libuv` 1.52.1, `luv` 1.52.1-0)

Related: #25575 (macOS hang inside `loop_close` at a different point — `uv__fsevents_close` semaphore wait; closed without repro).

comment_data.body:
I can reproduce this fairly reliably on Linux, with a different failure mode: a hard SIGSEGV instead of the CPU spin, but the same call path through `loop_close`.

Environment:
- Arch Linux, kernel 7.1.11-arch1-1, x86_64
- Neovim v0.12.5-1 (RelWithDebInfo), built 2026-08-24, installed 2026-08-28
- LuaJIT 2.1.1787165859+1ee778a-1 (Arch's `luajit` package)
- libuv 1.52.1-2
- Crashes started the day the neovim 0.12.5 package landed; 24 coredumps collected since via `coredumpctl`

Backtrace (symbolicated via debuginfod, crashing thread, SIGSEGV / SEGV_MAPERR):
```
#0 lua_rawgeti      (libluajit-5.1.so.2 + 0x263d2)
#1 luaL_unref       (libluajit-5.1.so.2 + 0x6d277)
#2 <no symbol>      (libluv.so.1 + 0x15f7e)
#3 uv_run           (libuv.so.1 + 0x16685)
#4 loop_close       (nvim + 0x17587f)
#5 os_exit          (nvim + 0x24558f)
#6 getout           (nvim + 0x245787)
```
So instead of `uv_walk` spinning forever, the final `uv_run` drain fires a libuv close callback that calls `luaL_unref` on a reference that's already gone, and `lua_rawgeti` reads unmapped memory. Might be the same handle-queue corruption described in this issue, just landing on garbage that segfaults instead of garbage that loops.

The common factor for me is an attached LSP client at quit time, not any specific server: I get this with both `rust_analyzer` and Haskell's LSP.

```sh
nvim --headless -c 'edit some/file.rs' -c 'sleep 800m' -c 'wq'
```

Run 15 times with my full config (LSP servers wired up through `vim.lsp.enable`, a couple dozen plugins), letting the client attach and settle for 800ms before quitting:

- 7 / 15 runs (47%) segfault on `:wq`
- 0 / 15 runs crash with `nvim --clean -u NONE` doing the same edit-and-quit cycle, no LSP involved
- 0 / 15 runs crash on a plain `.txt` file under the full config, where no LSP client ever attaches
- 0 / 8 runs crash if every client is stopped before quitting:
  ```lua
  for _, c in ipairs(vim.lsp.get_clients()) do vim.lsp.stop_client(c.id, true) end
  ```

So it's not plugin-specific or server-specific. It needs a live LSP client, and therefore a live libuv handle/timer owned by that client, at the moment `getout()` runs. Stopping clients first avoids it every time in my testing, which lines up with the handle-queue theory here.

Can share the full core dump or run more variations if that narrows down the corruption source. At least this gives something above "hundreds of stress attempts, zero reproductions."
please try nightly / latest master. bug reports from 1500 commits ago (0.12.x) are less helpful.

Tried this on nightly, `NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1511+g5209695703`, LuaJIT 2.1.1787165859.

Still reproducible. Same headless test as before, stock config, no local workarounds:

```sh
nvim --headless -c 'edit some/file.rs' -c 'sleep 800m' -c 'wq'
```

15 runs, 3 crashed (about 20%, versus 47% on stable 0.12.5 with the same test), 0 crashed with `--clean`.

Two of those three gave a fully symbolicated backtrace (this build isn't stripped, so no debuginfod needed), and it points at a specific site: closing a libuv thread handle during the final teardown drain.

```
#0 lua_rawgeti                  (nvim + 0x480b95)
#1 luaL_unref                   (nvim + 0x492efc)
#2 luv_thread_notify_close_cb   (nvim + 0x433305)
#3 uv__finish_close             (nvim + 0x4e84a1)
#4 loop_close                   (nvim + 0x19805b)
#5 event_teardown               (nvim + 0x2651ca)
#6 getout                       (nvim + 0x26538e)
```

I bisected this down to a specific plugin: `ms-jpq/coq_nvim`. It's the only one of about 70 plugins I have installed that calls `vim.uv.new_thread` anywhere in its source (`lua/coq/lib/worker/frame_transport.lua`, `M.spawn_worker`, which dumps a Lua closure with `string.dump` and runs it on a real OS thread via `vim.uv.new_thread({}, function(d, ...) load(d)(...) end, dumped, ...)`). With coq_nvim's plugin lines commented out of my config (everything else, including LSP setup, unchanged and verified still loading), the crash rate went from 2/15 to 0/15 in the same test. So the closing thread handle in the backtrace is very likely one of coq_nvim's worker threads.

I also tried a local workaround that force-stops every attached LSP client on `VimLeavePre` before quitting. On stable 0.12.5 that took my crash rate from about 50% to 0. On nightly it only reduced it (2/15 instead of 3/15), and one of those crashes came through a different path: stopping the client fires a deferred `LspDetach` autocmd, which triggered a plugin's statusline redraw, which called `os_breakcheck`, which re-entered the event loop mid-teardown, and landed in the exact same three innermost frames. So the actual bug looks like it's in the closing-thread/Lua-ref lifecycle itself, not tied to any one call site that reaches it.

Happy to attach the full core dumps for any of these runs. Since coq_nvim isn't the only plugin in the wild that spawns `uv.new_thread` workers for background computation, this is probably reproducible with other plugins that do the same thing.

title: loop_close() spins at 100% CPU inside uv_walk() (cyclic libuv handle queue); 2s teardown timeout bypassed
